# The otoform pipeline

Two stages. Stage 1 is expensive (images) and runs once; stage 2 is cheap
(1-D signals) and can be re-run with other settings.

## Stage 1: image to contour and signature

Unit: `process_image(path, method, threshold, k, grid_size, n_points)`.
Batch: `process_directory(dir, ...)`.

| Step | Function | Input | Output | Attributes carried out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `jpeg::readJPEG` | `path` | `img`, h x w x 3 in [0, 1] | - |
| 2 | `to_gray` | `img` | `g`, h x w luma (Rec. 709) in [0, 1] | - |
| 3 | `binarize(g, method, threshold, L = 256)` | `g` | list: `bw` (logical, `TRUE` = object), `threshold` (quantised scale), `separability`, `inverted`, `status` | - |
| 4 | `Conte` | `bw` | `raw`, N x 2 pixel coordinates, counter-clockwise | - |
| 5 | `resample_arc(raw, grid_size = 4096)` | `raw` | `fine`, 4096 x 2 | (check) |
| 6 | `smoothout(fine, k = 128)` | `fine` | `smooth`, 4096 x 2 | (check) |
| 7 | `rotation(smooth)` | `smooth` | `rotated`, centred on the vertex mean, major axis on x | `theta`, `center`, `anisotropy`, `status` |
| 8 | `anchor_rostrum(rotated, n_points = 512)` | `rotated` | `points`, 512 x 2 in pixels, rostrum at index 1 | `status`, `s_star`, `delta`, `perimeter` |
| 9 | `normalize_area(points)` | `points` | `norm`, unit area | `perimeter`, `s_star` rescaled; `area` (px^2) added |
| 10 | `centroid_distance(norm)` | `norm` | `r`, length 512, dimensionless | `centroid` |

`process_image()` returns: `file`, `raw`, `points`, `theta`, `status`, `msg`,
`threshold`, `separability`, `inverted`, `r`, `area`, `method`, `k`. The error
branch returns the same names with `NULL`/`NA`.

`points` (pixels) is the archival contour: it is what gets exported and
plotted, and what measurements will be computed from. `r` is the input of
stage 2. Attributes are provenance, never a data source.

### What the user calls, and what comes out

User-facing API: `process_directory()`. Everything else is internal or
documented for method comparison.

`process_directory(dir, out_dir = file.path(dir, "otoform"), overlay = FALSE,
chunk_size = 50, J = NULL, ...)` processes every JPEG in `dir` (stage 1, in
blocks, parallel if a `future` plan is set), decomposes every signature
(stage 2) and writes, in `out_dir`, one folder per locality next to the
images:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `log.csv` | one row per image, successful or not: `status`, `msg`, binarisation settings, `n_components`, `area_ratio`, `area`, `theta`; appended after each block |
| `contours.csv` | long, one row per vertex: `file`, `i` (rostrum at 1), `x`, `y`. **Aligned** contour: pixel units, centred on the area centroid, major axis on x; not the position in the image (`theta`, `center` in the log and `to_image()` map it back). 4 decimals |
| `signature.csv` | wide, one row per otolith: `r_001 ... r_512`, dimensionless, full precision |
| `wavelet_c6.csv` | wide: coarse approximation `c6_001 ... c6_512` |
| `wavelet_w1.csv` ... `wavelet_w6.csv` | wide: details `wj_001 ... wj_512`, one file per level; `signature = c6 + w1 + ... + w6` exactly |
| `results.rds`, `wavelets.rds` | the full R lists of both stages |
| `overlay/<file>.png` | only with `overlay = TRUE`: image with `points` (red dots), `raw` (grey), rostrum (green) and centroid (black); `export_overlay()` |

All CSV files: comma-separated, point decimal, UTF-8, header row
(`write.csv`). Open them in Excel through *Data → From Text/CSV* with an
English locale, or the point decimal is mangled. Wide files share the `file`
column, so levels are combined with a `merge` by `file`; `log.csv` says which
rows to exclude. The source images are never modified or copied.

## Stage 2: signature to wavelet decomposition

Unit: `atrous_b3(r, J)`. Batch: `process_contours(res, J = 6)`.

| Step | Function | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | `atrous_b3(r, J = NULL)` | `r` | `c[[1]]..c[[J + 1]]` approximations (`c[[1]]` is `r`), `w[[1]]..w[[J]]` details, `w[[j]] = c[[j]] - c[[j + 1]]`; reconstruction is exact: `c[[J + 1]] + sum(w)` equals the signature |

Descriptors derived from `w` are not decided yet (level energies vs.
coefficients); see Pending.

## Vocabulary

One name per object, everywhere:

| Name | Object |
|---|---|
| `path` | file path |
| `img` | RGB array from `readJPEG` |
| `g` | luma matrix in [0, 1] |
| `bw` | logical mask, `TRUE` = object |
| `raw` | traced contour, pixels |
| `xy` | any N x 2 contour matrix (function arguments) |
| `points` | final contour, pixels, 512 x 2 |
| `norm` | `points` normalised to unit area |
| `r` | centroid-distance signature |
| `c`, `w` | approximations and details of `atrous_b3` |
| `N`, `k`, `J`, `L`, `threshold` | number of points, smoothing, levels, grey levels, threshold on the quantised scale |

`process_*` family: `process_image` (one image), `process_directory` (many
images), `process_contours` (many signatures).

## Decisions and their justification

- **Otsu by default.** On the 10 reference images Otsu picks 63-88 (0.25-0.35
  in [0, 1]) with separability 0.93-0.96. A fixed cut at 0.5 (`threshold =
  127`) was ~50% above the optimum and produced holes and 5/10 wrong contours.
  shapeR's default 0.2 corresponds to `threshold = 50`.
- **Threshold on the quantised scale.** Same axis as Otsu's `k*`; `threshold`
  is the last level of the low class; a cut at `c` in [0, 1] is
  `floor(c * (L - 1) - 0.5)`.
- **Normalisation by area**, last geometric step, `sqrt(A)` scaling; original
  area kept as a covariate.
- **Area centroid**, not vertex mean: on the 9 reference contours the two
  differ by 0.036-0.077 (unit area), i.e. 30-65 px; the shift is
  shape-dependent (rostrum).
- **Number of levels: `J = max_levels(N)`.** The B3 kernel at level j spans
  `2^(j+2) - 3` points. Half-turn criterion: the deepest level must not span
  more than half the closed contour, so no detail compares a point with the
  opposite side (`2^(J+2) - 3 <= N/2`): 6 for N = 512, 7 for 1024, 5 for 256.
  The rule lives in one function and every default is `NULL`; an explicit `J`
  is accepted up to the full-contour bound (`<= N`, 7 for 512) and rejected
  beyond it.
- **Region-based geometry.** Area for normalisation, area centroid for centring
  and for `r`, area second moments for the principal axes (internal
  `polygon_moments()`), so no reference depends on boundary sampling and the
  same centroid is used by `rotation()` and `centroid_distance()`. `theta` is
  restricted to (-90, 90]: the 180-degree ambiguity is resolved by the
  photographic protocol (rostrum to the right) and not checked.
- **Batch processing in blocks, parallel on demand.** `process_directory()`
  processes images in blocks of `chunk_size` with `future.apply::future_lapply()`
  and appends the log after each block. The user sets the plan
  (`future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)`); the package never does.
  Measured on 9.2 Mpx images (2383 x 3840): 4.0 s/image sequential
  (to_gray 0.7, binarize 1.0, keep_largest 2.1, Conte 0.3; everything after
  Conte 0.05); 0.64 s/image effective with 4 workers (200 images in 128 s);
  8 workers give no further gain (memory-bound). Parallel and sequential runs
  produce identical logs. The overlay adds 2.3 s/image and stays off for bulk
  runs; flagged images are drawn afterwards with `write_overlay()`.
- **Visual QC on a 200-image sample** (one locality): 200/200 traced,
  `area_ratio` 0.998-1.089, Otsu thresholds 92-111, `theta` -8 to -2 degrees.
  The images with wrong contours (translucent otoliths, dirt, lighting) were
  those flagged by the extremes of `area_ratio` and `n_components`: the log
  does not decide, it ranks images for visual inspection. Such images are
  excluded and documented, not fixed in code; the remedy is the photographic
  protocol.
  - **Deliverables as plain text.** CSV over xlsx (binary, 1 048 576-row limit,
  locale-dependent) and over "txt" (no defined separator). Coordinates rounded
  to 4 decimals (sub-pixel anchoring is good to ~0.01 px); signatures and
  coefficients at full precision. One file per wavelet level, so a single
  level is a single read. Verified: the signature read from `signature.csv`
  equals the sum of the seven level files read from disk (1e-15).

## Pending (tracked as GitHub issues)

- `Conte` seeds at the image centre: ANE1724 traces a 10-pixel speck with
  `status = "ok"`. Fix: largest connected component (+ hole filling) before
  `Conte`. shapeR solves the same failure with a manual `mouse.click`.
- Area invariant (polygon area vs. mask area) in `process_image()`, so that
  `status` detects the case above.
- `measure_contour(points, cal)`: calibrated area, length, width, perimeter,
  roundness, from `points`.
- Export of `r` next to the coordinates.
- Descriptor choice (energies vs. coefficients).
- Cosmetics: `s_star`/`delta` carry a stray name `"x"`; `theta` reported in
  [0, 2*pi).
- Tests: exact reconstruction of `atrous_b3`; `normalize_area`;
  `polygon_centroid` on triangle and square.
- `keep_largest()` takes 2.1 of 4.0 s per 9 Mpx image: label a downsampled
  mask first, then crop and label at full resolution inside the bounding box.
- `to_gray()` and `binarize()` make redundant full-image passes (~0.5 s).
- A `qc.csv` next to `log.csv` with the human verdict per image, to measure
  whether rules on `area_ratio` / `n_components` predict wrong contours.
